mappings.name: transfer accepted (202, empty body — the id is the caller's), and only with a disbursement-scoped bearer

why: MTN's Disbursements refund. 202 with an empty body, exactly as requesttopay
answers on the charge path -- accepted, NOT settled; the outcome is read back
from GET /disbursement/v1_0/transfer/{referenceId}, a call vpay does not make
because the port has no refund status read (docs/flows/adapter-mtn-momo.md).
why-both-headers-are-matched: This is the whole point of the mapping, and both matchers are CONTRACTS.
The bearer: MTN's two products have separately scoped tokens. The stubs mint a
different string from each token endpoint, so matching the disbursement one
here is what tells 'the adapter minted a Disbursements token' from 'the
adapter asked the wrong token endpoint'. Point token::mint at
/collection/token/ and this mapping stops matching -- measured, 3 cases fail.
CORRECTED ON REVIEW, 2026-09-15. This note also claimed that removing Product
from Credentials::fingerprint stops the mapping matching. It does NOT: measured,
the whole suite stays green at 67/67, and so it does with the adapter's two
cache slots collapsed into one, and so it does with BOTH removed together. The
reason is in this file: the suite gives each product a DIFFERENT subscription
key and API key, so the two fingerprints differ with or without the product
discriminator and the cache never collides. The bug those guards exist for needs
a deployment that pasted IDENTICAL credentials into both halves, which this
suite never constructs. It is held by two unit tests in vpay-adapter-mtn-momo
(a_collections_bearer_is_never_served_to_a_disbursement and
a_products_bearer_is_stored_where_only_that_product_can_read_it) and by nothing
here.
The subscription key: likewise for the per-product Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key.
An adapter that read `credentials.subscription_key` for a transfer would send
the Collections key at a Disbursements endpoint, which in production is a
401 and here is a 404.
what-is-assumed: EVERYTHING ON THIS PATH. Nothing in this repository has ever called MTN's
Disbursements product, in sandbox or anywhere else, and MTN's portal serves
no OpenAPI schema document for it (docs/flows/adapter-mtn-momo.md, re-checked
2026-09-11). The path, the 202, the empty body and the request shape are a
transcription of MTN's published Transfer operation, which mirrors
RequestToPay with `payee` in place of `payer`. A stub faithful to that
documentation but not to the rail would pass every case that drives it.

mappings.name: transfer: a payee the rail has no record of

why: The decline a refund reaches that a charge does not: the money is going TO
this number, so 'the rail has no such party' is about the payee.
Selected on $.payee.partyId rather than on a reference, and that is the
assertion: a mapping keyed on the reference would still match an adapter that
sent `payer` instead of `payee`, or that sent the CHARGE's payer_ref as the
party. 237600000404 is the account-holder family's 'no record' number,
reused so a reader can look it up in one table.

mappings.name: transfer: a reference the rail has already seen

why: The adapter must read this as an accepted transfer, not as an error: after a
crash between the send and the commit, a retry has to be able to hear 'I
already have this instruction' without paying the payee twice.
Correct ONLY under the invariant in Adapter::refund's doc comment -- that the
reference is the REFUND's provider_reference_id and not the charge's. If a
future POST /v1/refunds handler passes the charge's, every partial refund
after the first lands here and is reported succeeded with no money moved.
That is recorded in RFC-0003 rather than assumed away.

mappings.name: transfer: 500 that is really our misconfiguration

jsonBody.message: The target environment is not allowed for this API user

metadata.why: MTN's biggest wart applies to the money-out path too: a logical error arrives as HTTP 500 with a code in the body, and this one is our own YAML. ProviderError::Config, so the poll ladder stops instead of retrying forever.

mappings.name: transfer: 307 whose Location must never be requested

why: requesttopay.json's 307 mapping, on the path where following one is worst: a
307 replays the request BODY, and this body carries the PAYEE'S PHONE NUMBER
as well as the Disbursements subscription key and the bearer. vpay_provider's
clients are built with redirect::Policy::none(), so the adapter must see this
itself and answer Malformed.
The Location is the same same-host path requesttopay.json's is, so the
existing `the Location is never requested` mapping (in that file) answers it
and the __admin request journal is the witness.
